events.title: AWK created at Bell Labs
events.summary: Alfred Aho, Peter Weinberger, and Brian Kernighan created AWK in 1977 — a pattern-action language for text processing on Unix.
events.about: AWK scans lines of text, matches patterns, and runs actions — ideal for log analysis, column extraction, and quick reports. `awk '{print $1}' access.log` became a daily sysadmin habit. Perl, Lua, and countless one-liners inherited AWK's field-splitting and regex model.

narrative.whyChosen: AWK defined the pattern-action paradigm that shaped Unix scripting and influenced Perl.
narrative.whyImportant: It made structured text processing a first-class programming style on every Unix system.
narrative.problemSolved: C programs were overkill for simple columnar reports; sed alone could not express arithmetic and structured control flow.

sources.title: GNU Awk Manual — original awk written in 1977 at Bell Labs

events.title: Brian Kernighan co-creates AWK
events.summary: Brian Kernighan co-designed AWK in 1977 with Aho and Weinberger — the pattern-action language for text processing.
events.about: AWK's columnar field model and regex patterns influenced Perl, Ruby, and every log-parsing one-liner. Kernighan's 'The C Programming Language' and 'Software Tools' shaped how programmers learn Unix.

narrative.whyChosen: AWK made structured text processing a first-class scripting task.
narrative.whyImportant: It influenced a generation of scripting languages and CLI culture.
narrative.problemSolved: Ad-hoc shell pipelines could not easily handle columnar report data.

events.title: Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman invent RSA
events.summary: Ron Rivest, Adi Shamir, and Leonard Adleman invented the RSA public-key algorithm at MIT in 1977 — enabling encryption and digital signatures at scale.
events.about: RSA turned public-key theory into a practical algorithm used in TLS certificates, SSH host keys, and code signing for decades. Their 1978 Communications of the ACM paper spread RSA beyond academia into commercial security products.

narrative.whyChosen: RSA became the most widely deployed public-key algorithm of the pre-quantum era.
narrative.whyImportant: It made digital signatures and encrypted key transport practical for software systems.
narrative.problemSolved: Public-key cryptography needed a concrete algorithm implementable on 1970s hardware.

events.title: John Backus receives Turing Award
events.summary: John Backus won the 1977 ACM Turing Award for contributions to Fortran and functional programming — including the Backus–Naur Form.
events.about: Backus led the IBM team that created Fortran and later argued for functional programming in his Turing lecture. BNF became the standard notation for describing programming language syntax.

narrative.whyChosen: Backus shaped both practical compilers and formal language specification.
narrative.whyImportant: Fortran proved high-level languages could match hand-coded assembly performance.
narrative.problemSolved: Scientists needed faster ways to program computers than machine code.
